ledger.claim: POL-NS-02 deems a driver to have ARRIVED only where the trace holds at least three consecutive fixes, each reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the arrival radius of the pickup pin - 50 m for the STANDARD zone class this trip carries. The arrival test run on this trip's trace returns qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0 fixes lasting 0.0 seconds across all 100 driver fixes, so there is no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes before the 19:18:19 cancellation. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, and under POL-NS-02 the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The fee also fails POL-NS-01 limb (c). The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the free waiting period in force of 180 seconds - trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and the derived threshold minimum_dwell_sec of 180 for STANDARD - a shortfall of 180 seconds. Limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 19:11:37, so the 6.7 minutes the trip_record shows between the tap and the 19:18:19 cancellation is not dwell and cannot cure the shortfall.

On the shortfall alone POL-NS-06 is decisive: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, the cancellation fee 'is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. That removes the rider's own whereabouts from the question. The rider's device track places it 891.7 to 898.7 m from the pin throughout, stationary, and POL-NS-04 is not available to the rider because the chat log holds only the driver's message - but neither point bears on the fee, because POL-NS-01's four limbs contain no rider-presence element and POL-NS-06 makes the refund independent of it. The waiting period is the consideration the fee was paid for; it was not served.

The driver cannot repair the shortfall by accumulating dwell across separate in-geofence intervals: POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits that only where a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road and the waiting period. The advisory artifact for this pickup is MISSING - weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload - and I disclose that impairment; the claim rests on the absence itself, which is citable. The derived accumulation block records run_count 0 and limb (i) unavailable both because there is no second in-geofence interval and because a MISSING traffic_advisory cannot be asserted to anyone's benefit. There is no lawful-impossibility excuse here, and no accumulation route to 180 seconds.

The driver's counterparty statement ('I was at the pin for over six minutes') and his 19:11:57 chat message ('im at the pickup point') are assertions, not the measurement POL-NS-02 requires. The trace's own derived driver_track reports a mean distance of 2412.3 m from the pin and a maximum of 8833.3 m, with recorded speeds reaching 62.8 km/h, and the arrival test finds no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the 16.7 minutes it covers. A message saying he was at the pin cannot supply the three consecutive admissible in-radius fixes he did not have, and the statement is contradicted by his own telemetry.

The trip's arrival marker is a driver button press - platform_policy.arrival_marker is 'BUTTON' - so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed arrival route does not cover it and it stands or falls on the exported trace; POL-NS-12 expressly excludes a BUTTON marker. That export covers the arrival moment with no gap (100.0% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0) and still contains no qualifying in-geofence fix. On POL-NS-05's recomputed clock, which runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, the corrected dwell is 0 seconds and the full refund stands with no compensation payable; and where the marker is held false, limb (ii) additionally requires a false-arrival event to be recorded against the driver in the ruling's referrals.

Even if the driver were treated as having held position outside the arrival radius but within the 400 m ceiling, POL-NS-03 does not make this fee chargeable - it confirms the fee is refunded to the rider in full - and it yields the driver no compensation on this record. The only payment it provides is the limb (ii) goodwill of 50 percent, which requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points to be 2 or more, and this trip records exactly 1 registered pickup point; limb (i), the only other allocation, denies compensation. In any event the record establishes no stationary dwell of the required length within 400 m, so the clause is not reached at all.

Nothing in this bundle is impaired for policy purposes, so no down-weighting or escalation follows. The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100.0% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, 100 fixes at a 10 s cadence within the emitted interval, and both driver and rider tracks present; the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 1; and the fare line of 4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, the net figure the resolution rule produces, so POL-NS-08(d) is satisfied. No limb of POL-NS-08 fires, and POL-GEN-02's cap on confidence is not engaged - the finding rests on artifacts at weight 1.0.

The rider filed this dispute, so returning the fee is a rider win under POL-GEN-03. The contested amount is exactly the cancellation-fee line: the fare breakdown charges 4.50 as the cancellation fee, with base, distance, time, platform and waiting-time lines all at 0.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The remedy is a full refund of that 4.50 under POL-NS-06, and no driver compensation, because POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, which is not the case here.

The record carries the platform's own arrival event for this trip: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 19:11:37 and the wait timer started two seconds later at 19:11:39, with the trace and the trip record ordered consistently (earliest GPS fix 19:02:47, trip cancelled 19:18:19, no gap in the trace). Limb (a) of POL-NS-01 requires nothing more than a driver 'arrived' event in the trip_record, and it is there.

The trip was terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW at 19:18:19, at a time after the arrival marker; the trip was never started (started_at is null), ended_at is null and the event chain records no boarding event. Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is made out, and RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three codes that limb expressly recognises.

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. The 300-second STANDARD figure in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec is legacy: the fee_schedule resolution rule applies minimum_dwell_sec only to records authored before policy version 2, and this record carries a platform_policy block, so 180 seconds is the minimum. The platform's own wait clock ran 402 seconds from wait_timer_started at 19:11:39 to the 19:18:19 cancellation, 222 seconds beyond the period in force.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider, and the Judge should not read it as if it did. Limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent by the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log holds exactly one message — the driver's — so there is no rider message to quote. Limb (c) requires the rider's device to sit within the 100 m STANDARD rider_presence_radius_m for the majority of qualifying fixes, and the rider_track's 75 fixes between 19:08:28 and 19:19:31 sit between 891.7 m and 898.7 m from the pickup pin with rider_qualifying_fix_count at 0. Limb (c) is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes rather than undecidable, so POL-NS-11 has no work to do here.

The record describes a rider who was not at the pickup point and went silent there. The driver's only message, 'im at the pickup point', was sent at 19:11:57, delivered at 19:11:58 and read at 19:12:27; the rider never replied in the chat, never placed an in-app voice call (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty), and never moved at all — every speed on the rider track is 0.0 kph across the whole 19:08:28 to 19:19:31 window, with the device held roughly 890 to 899 m from the pin. That is the failure to appear that limb (d) of POL-NS-01 describes, and it corroborates the RIDER_NO_SHOW code instead of exposing a mis-selected one.

The money line is clean and there is nothing for POL-NS-08 to discount. The fare_breakdown cancellation_fee of SGD 4.50 equals the net cancellation fee in force for this trip (platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50, and the same figure in fee_schedule.defaults), payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and the ledger reconciles to total_charged 4.5 with no waiting-time line to refund. No limb (a) to (d) of POL-NS-08 fires, and every artifact in the bundle carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so no finding on this record need be discounted.

If the fee stands, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at SGD 3.60 — 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 net fee, stated in the fare_breakdown's own money block as driver_compensation — and the anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4 the clause requires, and 1 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 130 is a rate of 0.008, below the 0.08 threshold. No other profile field enters that test. Under POL-GEN-03 the emitted ruling where compensation is paid is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring the compensation figure, and it is error to emit NO_ACTION here.

If the Judge cannot settle arrival on this record, the disposition is escalation, not a refund. The platform's telemetry records the arrival event, the wait timer and a 402-second wait (wait_time_min 6.7), while the gps_trace's derived arrival block returns 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes, a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds and a 180-second shortfall — and the same artifact's driver_track reports a minimum distance of 0.0 m against a mean of 2412.3 m. Two admissible artifacts therefore point opposite ways on the very facts the fee depends on. POL-NS-05, the clause that resolves a false arrival marker, cannot be run because the record states neither the driver's distance from the pin nor his speed at the 19:11:37 marker; and POL-NS-12 cannot carry the platform's arrival and wait events either, because arrival_marker is BUTTON and not GPS_AUTO. That is precisely the conflict POL-NS-09(b) exists for, and the disputed SGD 4.50 should be held pending human review rather than refunded.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver — this is the ruling on trip TRP-02722. The disputed SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the fee does not stand. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four of its limbs hold, and the driver's side must carry every one of them. Limb (a) holds: EV-TRIP-02722 carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 19:11:37. Limb (d) holds: the trip was terminated by the driver at 19:18:19 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, started_at and ended_at are null, and the event chain records no boarding event. Limbs (b) and (c) fail on the GPS trace.

Limb (b) reads the arrival test of POL-NS-02: the driver is deemed to have arrived only where EV-GPS-02722 contains at least three consecutive fixes, each reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the arrival radius of the pickup pin — 50 m for this trip's STANDARD zone class. That trace is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, covers 100.0% of the window with max_gap_sec 0.0, and returns qualifying_fix_count 0 with a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds across all 100 driver fixes. No qualifying in-radius fix exists anywhere in the 15 minutes preceding the 19:18:19 cancellation, so limb (b) fails and POL-NS-02 gives the rider a full refund of the cancellation fee. Limb (c) reads the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and that dwell is 0.0 seconds against the free waiting period in force of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; the 300-second STANDARD figure in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec is legacy and does not apply to a record carrying a platform_policy block) — a shortfall of 180 seconds. POL-NS-06 then applies in terms: a dwell shorter than the waiting period is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'.

Driver, on your arguments. I accept that you tapped 'I'm Here' at 19:11:37 and that the platform's wait clock ran 6.7 minutes (wait_time_min) from the arrival tap to the cancellation, and I accept the rider was not at the pin: the rider's device held position 891.7–898.7 m away throughout, sent no message, made no in-app call, and never replied to your 19:11:57 message (read 19:12:27). None of that makes the fee chargeable. Limb (c)'s clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, so the minutes you waited after the tap are not dwell under POL-NS-01; and POL-NS-06 makes the refund independent of the rider's presence, so the rider's own failure to appear does not save the fee. Your counterparty statement ('I was at the pin for over six minutes') and your chat message are assertions of the very fact the trace is required to measure, and they are not borne out by your own telemetry (driver track mean distance 2412.3 m from the pin, maximum 8833.3 m, speeds up to 62.8 km/h, closest approach 0 m but no sustained in-geofence dwell). Under POL-NS-02, fixes that do not meet the 25 m accuracy filter are ignored and count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, so the closest approach of 0 m does not establish the consecutive admissible in-radius readings limb (b) requires.

Driver, on escalation. I do not escalate under POL-NS-09(b). That ground needs two admissible artifacts that contradict each other directly on arrival, dwell or rider presence and no clause that resolves the conflict. The 'arrived' event is a status you set, and POL-NS-01 limb (a) reads it only as the existence of that event; the measurement of your position is the trace, and POL-NS-12 expressly does not extend the platform-confirmed-arrival route to a driver-pressed (BUTTON) marker — this trip's arrival_marker is BUTTON — so the arrival question is decided by POL-NS-02, which gives a definite answer on this record. Nor does the trace affirmatively place you 300 m or more from the pin: its closest approach to the pin is 0 m, and the record states neither your distance from the pin nor your speed at 19:11:37. POL-NS-05 therefore cannot be run in either direction, and no false-arrival finding is made. POL-NS-07 consequently never engages: it pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, so the SGD 3.60 payout in the fare breakdown's money block does not arise, and the anti-farming check (no_show_terminations_30d 1, rate 0.008 against completed_trips_30d 130) does not need to be reached.

Rider, on your arguments. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you — the chat log holds only the driver's message, so there is no locating or coordinating message from you, and your device's 75 fixes all lie outside the 100 m rider-presence radius — and POL-NS-11 has no work to do because limb (c) fails affirmatively rather than being undecidable. The refund does not depend on that; it follows from the unserved waiting period under POL-NS-06, as you argued. I accept that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02722-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-NS-06(i)'s route to sum separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable; there were no in-geofence intervals to sum in any event (run_count 0). I decline the POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral for the reason given above — the marker cannot be held false on this record — and I record no false-arrival event against the driver. The open question of the driver's exact position at 19:11:37 is noted here rather than in a referral.

Weights and confidence. Nothing the ruling rests on is impaired: EV-GPS-02722, EV-TRIP-02722 and EV-FARE-02722 each carry weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, and the fare line of 4.50 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd under POL-NS-08(d), so no limb of POL-NS-08 fires. The POL-GEN-02(2) cap is therefore 1.0 and I set confidence at 0.85. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 it executes automatically on issue; the appeal route under POL-GEN-04 remains open to either party.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
